pr_title: feat: Bind keyboard events to the current  excalidraw container and add handleKeyboardGlobally prop to allow host to bind to document
pr_body:
fixes https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/3405
Also fixes handling keyboard events for individual excalidraw container when [multiple excalidraw](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/issues/3043) rendered
- [x] Keyboard shortcuts are no more binded after modal rendered so fix it.
- [x] Add handleKeyboardGlobally prop to allow host to bind to document
- [x] Testing
- [x] update changelog

✅ Preview: [https://excalidraw-git-aakansha-keyboard-excalidraw.vercel.app](https://excalidraw-git-aakansha-keyboard-excalidraw.vercel.app)
Was trying to break it and in the process fixed some cases.

I'm ambivalent about [`2c8ec6b` (#3430)](https://github.com/excalidraw/excalidraw/pull/3430/commits/2c8ec6be8eff7d308591467fe2c33cfbca16138f) — on one hand it's good that the modal is specific to the component, on the other hand it effectively isn't a modal: at least not a modal for the host app, only only for the excalidraw component. May be ok for some use cases while not for the others (both in terms of UX and UI).

We should disable the focus outline on the containers we've added `tabIndex` to:

- excalidraw:
	
	![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/114283161-a3b80100-9a48-11eb-8a19-6d7b6d39c158.png)

- modals:
	
	![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5153846/114283168-a87cb500-9a48-11eb-9ee6-2c0de9267528.png)

More cases:

- [x] should focus the container after installing a library
- [x] should focus the container after closing error dialogs
- [x] should focus the container after clicking `confirm` of clear-library alert dialog (not sure why other alert dialogs work, or hitting `cancel`)

I bet there will be other cases. And we need to test other browsers.

> * [ ]  focus the container after installing library

it's focussing on `body` and the next tab will go to the library popup which should be fine?

> * [ ]  focus on error dialog close

It does focus on the error dialog close button when custom error dialog is rendered coz of autofocus attribute, which case it's not doing it?

> * [ ]  focus on clear-library alert dialog confirm (not sure why other alert dialogs work, or hitting `cancel`)

This is an issue in prod as well so wanted to fix this along with some other A11y fixes in a separate PR.

> it's focussing on `body` and the next tab will go to the library popup which should be fine?

What do you do you mean by next tab? Manually having to press `tab`? We should focus the editor automatically as we do with other cases so people don't have to tab.

> It does focus on the error dialog close button when custom error dialog is rendered coz of autofocus attribute, which case it's not doing it?

I mean after you close the dialog. May not affect all error dialogs, haven't checked.

> This is an issue in prod as well so wanted to fix this along with some other A11y fixes in a separate PR.

But prod doesn't introduce this PR's a11y regression. But sure, we can withstand a small period where it doesn't work correctly. EDIT: we may actually wanna keep excalidraw.com using document-level handler, so it won't be affected.
I'd still name `bindKeyGlobally` differently as this isn't descriptive. Calling it `handleKeysGlobally` should be fine.

> I'd still name `bindKeyGlobally` differently as this isn't descriptive. Calling it `handleKeysGlobally` should be fine.

`handlKeysGlobally` sounds more like a callback since it starts with handle (maybe it's just me), lets name it as `shouldHandleKeysGlobally` instead?

IMO it comes down to context. A `verb*` naming can be used both for booleans and methods, and we already do it e.g. with `detectScroll: boolean`. Usually, handlers use  `on*` scheme (which we again do for our public API, unlike in our codebase for some reason).

Ultimately, you have intellisense (even if you don't use TS), and even if not, users won't randomly use props without reading the docs first.

Whatever we do, I'd not use `should*` as that is unnecessary and we don't use this for other props.

I just wanted to use something short, but descriptive. `bindKeyGlobally` is weird: what `key`? Bind how?

I'd maybe correct myself and use `handleKeyboardGlobally` since `keys` is ambiguous again.

issue_context.title: Execute keyboard events only when inside excalidraw
issue_context.body:
Right now if we use any shortcut keys for example `cmd+/cmd-` to zoom in, there is no way to zoom in out the browser since the keyboard listener of excalidraw gets executed.

We need to make sure the keyboard events apply only when inside Excalidraw instance.

review_comments: this is too generic — can break at any time (+ isn't multi-component friendly)
this will be fixed when we start storing active element as discussed in separate PR and right now we are doing this at other places as well example collab button for manually focussing.
